newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, bellies end with sharp gains, firm cash.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, bellies end with sharp gains, firm cash.

text.p: CME hogs and pork bellies settled sharply higher Monday, with December hogs near limit gains on firm cash prices as well as profit taking on short positions, CME floor traders said.
Several key Midwestern cash hog markets reported sales at steady to higher prices Monday, which was enough to convince some speculators that the recent free-fall in hog prices was over, traders said.
"What we saw today was pent-up buying demand," one floor broker said. "People have been waiting to buy this market for such a long time."
Market observers said that half of the buying in Monday's trading was the short covering, while the other half was fresh buying spurred by ideas that a major market bottom had been hit last week.
The strong gains in futures sparked talk of a sharp pick-up in pork export sales volume, which fueled some of the session's gains, traders and analysts said.
However, CME traders with ties to the export markets reported no unusual activity and could not confirm a jump in pork sales.

Some of the strength in Monday's rally was also attributed to light hog marketings due to forecasts for rain in the western Corn Belt for Tuesday, traders said. They said farmers were quickly trying to finish up harvest before the next rain system moved in and were not marketing hogs.
Buying by commercial firm, Packers Trading, pushed the December contract through buy-stop orders near the open, floor sources said.
Pork bellies were also sharply higher, and rallied in sympathy with hog futures and on firm cash pork belly prices, CME traders said.

CME hogs ended up 0.325 to 1.900 cent lb, with December hogs up 1.425 cent at 53.875 cents and February up 1.900 at 73.825 cents. Pork bellies closed up 1.775 to 2.125 cent a lb, with February up 2.125 cents at $70.050.
